article.title: Break the ice
article.description: Meaning: to say or do something that relieves tension or awkwardness, especially when meeting people for the first time. Example: 'She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.' Common mistake: learners sometimes say 'break ice' without 'the'. Origin note: comes from ships literally breaking ice to allow passage.

generated.caption:
Ever felt that awkward silence when meeting new people? This is where 'break the ice' comes in! It means to say or do something to relieve tension or awkwardness, especially during first meetings. Just remember: always say 'the ice'!

For example: 'She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.'

generated.script: Ye 'break ice' aur 'break THE ice' mein confusion hota hai na? Toh 'break the ice' ka matlab hai ki jab aap pehli baar kisi se milte ho, aur wahan thodi tension ya awkwardness hoti hai, toh usko kam karne ke liye kuch bolna ya karna. For example, 'She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.' Matlab, usne ek joke sunaya taaki meeting mein sab comfortable feel karein. Toh next time awkwardness door karni ho toh hamesha bolo 'break THE ice', sirf 'break ice' nahi. Ab clear hai na? Comment mein batao aapne bhi kabhi ye mistake ki thi kya? slides.body: To 'break the ice' means to say or do something that helps relieve tension or awkwardness, especially when people are meeting for the first time. For instance, 'She told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.' It's important to remember that the correct idiom always includes the definite article 'the' – saying just 'break ice' is a common mistake. The phrase refers to overcoming the initial social barrier, much like how ships literally broke through ice to allow passage.
